sources.title: Daniel T. Gillespie, “Exact Stochastic Simulation of Coupled Chemical Reactions,” Journal of Physical Chemistry 81 (1977)
sources.locator: §§II.B–III.C, full 22-page PDF; joint event-time/channel calculation and direct stochastic simulation algorithm, PDF pp. 4–7 / journal pp. 2342–2346.
sources.support: The paper derives the reaction-event pair law and direct simulation procedure. Its chemical collision and mass-action model motivation is treated as model context only; the authored theorems prove the stochastic network model from its specified propensities.

contents.name: §II.B–II.C: stochastic event-time and reaction-channel probability derivation
contents.support: The source motivates the joint event law; the local lemma proves the independent exponential-clock formula completely.

contents.name: §III.C: direct method transforms one exponential and one uniform input into the next reaction event
contents.support: The carrier states the full typed input, selection rule, horizon and finite-budget statuses.

contents.name: §II.A: collision-volume derivation for physical gas-phase reaction propensities
contents.reason: This page takes propensity functions as mathematical model inputs and makes no claim that a physical chemical system obeys mass-action kinetics.

sources.title: David F. Anderson, Introduction to Stochastic Processes with Applications to Biology, complete course text
sources.support: This independent full course text treats CTMC holding times and explosion, reaction-network generators and random time changes, exact simulation algorithms, and a Poisson minimum-intensity coupling construction. Its coupling section also covers approximations; only the exact common/residual Poisson construction is used here.

contents.name: Chapter 6 §6.2, Proposition 6.2.2: summable exponential holding means imply finite explosion time
contents.support: The source provides the explosion criterion; the example proves the quadratic-rate case locally by computing the holding-time expectations.

contents.name: Chapter 6 §6.2, Example 6.2.3: pure-birth process with quadratic rates explodes
contents.support: The B item verifies the specified n-squared example with a complete finite-expectation proof.

contents.name: Chapter 7 §7.1.1: stochastic equations and basic reaction-network terminology
contents.support: The local definition states the state set, increments, propensities, admissibility and generator convention.

contents.name: Chapter 7 §7.1.4: reaction generator and forward equations
contents.support: The local theorem derives the finite-state generator from the event kernel, including zero-increment events.

contents.name: Chapter 7 §7.1.5: countable-state CTMCs built by random time changes
contents.support: The countable-state extension states its own properness and local rate hypotheses and proves non-explosion.

contents.name: Chapter 7 §7.2.1: stochastic simulation algorithm
contents.support: The carrier completes the algorithm with exact input domains and explicit incomplete and absorbing statuses.

contents.name: Chapter 7 §7.2.2: next-reaction method
contents.support: The carrier specifies every clock update and defines the associated random-time-change path.

contents.name: Chapter 7 §7.3.1: common Poisson component at the minimum of two rates and independent residual components
contents.support: The algorithm implements the per-channel shared minimum and one-sided residual rates; its theorem proves exact marginals.

contents.name: Chapter 7 §7.2.2: approximate integrated-hazard inversion route
contents.reason: This pair implements the separately proved bounded-envelope thinning branch; certified numerical root solving for integrated hazards is not part of this page.

sources.title: David F. Anderson and Thomas G. Kurtz, “Continuous Time Markov Chain Models for Chemical Reaction Networks,” complete survey
sources.locator: §§2.1–2.6, complete 44-page PDF; Poisson processes, CTMC random-time-change equations, thinning, martingale problems, forward equations and simulation, PDF pp. 5–16.
sources.support: This independent survey supplies full context for unit-rate Poisson clocks, random-time-change reaction models, thinning and the generator/martingale formulations. The survey itself states that much discussion is motivational; every cited probabilistic conclusion used here is separately proved in the local items or supplied by an exact published interface.

contents.name: §2.1: Poisson processes and independent increments
contents.support: The existing theorem supplies the precise finite-window ordered-event density used by the local simulation proofs.

contents.name: §2.2: continuous-time Markov chains and reaction-network random-time change
contents.support: The local algorithm defines the accumulated internal times and threshold refresh rule.

contents.name: §2.3: equivalence of stochastic equations and martingale problems
contents.support: The local theorem proves each count martingale clause from the constructed candidate process rather than assuming intensity alone suffices.

contents.name: §2.4: thinning of counting processes
contents.support: The local theorem proves survival and cause-specific first-event laws for Borel rates and general disjoint mark sets.

contents.name: §2.5: martingale problem and forward equation for Markov chains
contents.support: The finite-state theorem independently derives the generator by a small-time event calculation.

contents.name: §2.6: exact CTMC simulation by next-reaction and direct methods
contents.support: The local theorem proves equality of the event kernels and finite-horizon path laws.
